cards.v: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.
cards.a: Tell or write to one member: “Thank you—I see the Lord’s love in you.”

cards.v: In love of the brothers be tenderly affectionate to one another; in honor prefer one another,
cards.a: This Sunday, give the better seat, the first word, or the credit to someone else.

cards.v: Be of the same mind one toward another. Don’t set your mind on high things, but associate with the humble. Don’t be wise in your own conceits.
cards.a: Sit beside someone who is often overlooked and listen to them for ten minutes.

cards.v: So then, let’s follow after things which make for peace, and things by which we may build one another up.
cards.a: In a group chat or face to face, say one specific word that builds someone up—no “but” attached.

cards.v: Therefore accept one another, even as Christ also accepted you, to the glory of God.
cards.a: Invite a member very different from you (age, background, views) for coffee or tea.

cards.v: I myself am also persuaded about you, my brothers, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge, able also to admonish others.
cards.a: If there is something you have wanted to tell a brother or sister, pray for three days first, then speak gently and privately.

cards.v: Greet one another with a holy kiss. The assemblies of Christ greet you.
cards.a: Learn the names of three members this week and greet each by name next time you meet.

cards.v: that there should be no division in the body, but that the members should have the same care for one another.
cards.a: Find someone who has missed gatherings lately and message them: “I miss you, and I’m praying for you.”

cards.v: For you, brothers, were called for freedom. Only don’t use your freedom as an opportunity for the flesh, but through love be servants to one another.
cards.a: Do one task at church that no one will see and no one needs to thank you for.

cards.v: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
cards.a: Ask a member: “What is your heaviest burden right now? How can I help?”

cards.t: Bear with One Another in Love
cards.v: with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love,
cards.a: With a member who irritates you, choose today not to keep a record in your heart.

cards.v: And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
cards.a: Bring one thing you still hold onto before the Lord and say, “Lord, I choose to forgive.”

cards.v: subjecting yourselves to one another in the fear of Christ.
cards.a: In your next team discussion, hear others out fully before sharing your own view.

cards.v: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
cards.a: Write down three ways a co-worker is better than you, and tell them one of them.

cards.t: Do Not Lie to One Another
cards.v: Don’t lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old man with his doings,
cards.a: Today, no exaggerating or polishing—speak only what is true in your church conversations.

cards.v: bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
cards.a: If there is friction with someone, pray a blessing over them today and ask the Lord for a forbearing heart.

cards.v: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly; in all wisdom teaching and admonishing one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your heart to the Lord.
cards.a: Share a worship song that has encouraged you with one member, along with one line of what it meant to you.

cards.v: Therefore comfort one another with these words.
cards.a: Visit or call a member who is grieving—fewer explanations, more presence.

cards.v: Therefore exhort one another, and build each other up, even as you also do.
cards.a: Send an encouraging message to your small group leader or pastor, thanking them for their labor.

cards.v: but exhort one another day by day, so long as it is called “today”, lest any one of you be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
cards.a: Agree with your spiritual companion to send each other one verse every day this week.

cards.t: Provoke to Love and Good Works
cards.v: Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,
cards.a: Invite a member to do one good work together—a visit, a meal, welcoming a newcomer.

cards.t: Do Not Speak Against One Another
cards.v: Don’t speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother and judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.
cards.a: If you want to criticize someone today, pray for them instead; don’t talk about them behind their back for 24 hours.

cards.v: Don’t grumble, brothers, against one another, so that you won’t be judged. Behold, the judge stands at the door.
cards.a: Replace one complaint about the church with a word of thanks—and say it aloud.

cards.t: Confess and Pray for One Another
cards.v: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.
cards.a: Share one struggle honestly with a trusted spiritual companion, and pray for each other.

cards.v: Seeing you have purified your souls in your obedience to the truth through the Spirit in sincere brotherly affection, love one another from the heart fervently,
cards.a: For someone you “should love but find hard to love,” ask the Lord for love from the heart.

cards.v: Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
cards.a: This week open your home, or treat a member to a meal.

cards.v: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.
cards.a: Use one of your gifts or skills to meet a practical need for a member.

cards.v: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elder. Yes, all of you clothe yourselves with humility and subject yourselves to one another; for “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
cards.a: Ask a younger or older member for advice on something, and truly learn from them.

cards.v: If I then, the Lord and the Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another’s feet.
cards.a: Do a “low place” task—stacking chairs, washing dishes, cleaning—saying in your heart, “Lord, I follow you.”

cards.v: But if we walk in the light as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his Son cleanses us from all sin.
cards.a: Share honestly with a member what God did in you this week, and listen to theirs.

gifts.d: You make truth clear and help people understand and obey God’s Word.
gifts.s: Sunday school, discipleship classes, leading small group Bible study, children’s ministry lessons
q: I like organizing biblical truth so others can grasp it easily.
People often say I explain things clearly.
I’m willing to spend time preparing in order to teach others.

gifts.d: Your words encourage, comfort, and spur people on, helping the weary stand again.
gifts.s: Care visits, newcomer follow-up, one-on-one support, encouragement card ministry
q: When I see someone discouraged, I naturally want to encourage them.
After talking with me, people often feel strengthened to keep going.
I’m often prompted to send someone a word or a verse.

gifts.d: You gladly help with practical tasks so the whole body runs smoothly.
gifts.s: Ushering, setup, sound and media, meals, cleaning, transportation
q: I like practical work; when I see a need, I want to pitch in.
I’m glad to serve behind the scenes even if no one notices.
I would rather help with tasks than stand up front.

gifts.d: You are especially sensitive to suffering and gladly come alongside those in pain.
gifts.s: Visiting the sick, caring for seniors, grief support, serving the vulnerable
q: I easily sense other people’s pain.
I’m willing to stay with suffering people for a long time.
It moves me deeply when I see someone overlooked or weak.

gifts.d: You gladly and sincerely share resources to support the needs of God’s kingdom.
gifts.s: Giving, supporting missions and those in need, resource drives, finance team
q: When I see a need, my first thought is often “I can contribute.”
Giving money or goods away brings me joy.
I manage my resources carefully so I can help others more.

gifts.d: You see direction, rally people, and diligently lead a team forward.
gifts.s: Small group leader, ministry lead, project leader, team coordination
q: When a team lacks direction, I often naturally step up.
I can see the goal and persuade others to join in.
People often ask me, “What should we do next?”

gifts.d: You plan, organize, and manage details so ministry runs in order.
gifts.s: Administration, event planning, scheduling, records, bookkeeping
q: I like arranging things in good order.
I notice details and processes others miss.
Planning timelines and assigning tasks gives me satisfaction.

gifts.d: You make people feel welcomed and accepted, as if they have come home.
gifts.s: Welcoming newcomers, home groups, fellowship meals, welcome team
q: I like inviting people home or out for a meal.
I easily reach out to new people.
I enjoy helping strangers feel at ease.

gifts.d: You are often moved to pray at length for people, the church, and the city.
gifts.s: Prayer meetings, intercession team, prayer chain, praying for pastors
q: I often stop to pray when someone comes to mind.
Long seasons of prayer are a joy to me, not a burden.
I keep track of prayer requests and follow God’s answers.

gifts.d: You naturally share Jesus with unbelievers and help them come to know Him.
gifts.s: Outreach events, personal evangelism, seekers’ class, community outreach
q: I find it easy to talk about faith with friends who don’t believe.
Seeing someone come to faith is one of my greatest joys.
I often think about how to help people around me meet Jesus.

gifts.d: You are willing to care long-term for a group’s spiritual growth, like a shepherd with a flock.
gifts.s: Small group shepherding, spiritual parenting, discipleship mentoring, new believer care
q: I carry certain people’s spiritual condition on my heart over time.
I’m willing to spend time walking with someone as they slowly grow.
When someone strays or leaves, I want to go find them.

gifts.d: You express God’s beauty through art, design, music, or skilled craft.
gifts.s: Worship team, graphic design, media, decor, handcraft ministry
q: I love expressing faith through creativity, design, or music.
I have a craft or technical skill I want to use at church.
It moves me when beautiful work helps people know God more.

recon.safety: If this involves violence, sexual harassment or assault, spiritual abuse, financial misconduct, threats, or any crime, please do not face it alone, and you do not need to “go privately” first. Make sure you are safe, reach out to a trusted pastor, elder, or your church’s overseeing body, and contact the police or professional help when needed. Forgiveness is not silence, and reconciliation never means returning to danger.

steps.v: You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
steps.d: Remove the log from your own eye first. What is my part in this? How much pride, hurt, or judgment is in my heart?
q: What is my part in this?
What actually hurt me?
Do I want to win my brother—or win the argument?

steps.v: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
steps.d: Be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger. Give it at least one night. Bring your emotions to the Lord and ask the Spirit to govern your heart and mouth.
q: What am I feeling right now?
Am I willing to pray a blessing over them?
What is the Spirit reminding me of?

steps.v: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
steps.d: When it is just the two of you, speak humbly, specifically, and without accusation. The goal is to win your brother.
q: Can I apologize for my part first?
What is the one specific thing I need to say?
Am I ready to listen to their side?

steps.v: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
steps.d: If they will not listen, ask one or two mature, fair members whom both of you trust to come along—not to gang up, but to help you both see clearly.
q: Who do both of us trust?
Have I sincerely completed the previous step?

steps.v: If he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the assembly. If he refuses to hear the assembly also, let him be to you as a Gentile or a tax collector.
steps.d: If it is still unresolved, go through the church’s proper pastoral channels (pastors, elders)—not group chats or whispers.
q: Am I using the right channel?
Is my motive still restoration?

steps.v: bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
steps.d: Forgiveness lays down the right to collect the debt and leaves judgment to God. Trust can be rebuilt over time as there is repentance. When needed, you can forgive and still keep a safe distance.
q: Am I willing to say, “Lord, I choose to forgive”?
What healthy boundary do I need?

opens: I want to apologize for my part first: …
I care about our relationship, so I’d like to talk with you about something.
When … happened, I felt … . I’d like to hear your side.
I may have misunderstood you—could you help me understand?
Could we pray about this together?

fruits.d: Keeping my word where I serve

way.t: The Holy Spirit is my guide
way.q: Have I first asked the Holy Spirit about this ministry? Do I have His prompting and peace?
Is this biblical? Which truth am I understanding and obeying?
Am I serving with the heart of Jesus—a humble, self-giving life?
Am I serving in His authority and power, or in my own talent and experience?

way.t: Let Jesus receive all the glory
way.q: When it is done, who gets the glory? Will I give thanks in everything?
